request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
A couple of observations for the designers:

- The alert system worked really well. When Pirate-1 found the cave, the alert immediately let everyone else redirect without wasting further turns on their old routes. That felt like the key mechanic for coordinating after discovery.
- The noisy readings meant we couldn’t pinpoint the cave from a single set of starting digs, but the four starting corners plus shared readings narrowed the search to a small cluster. It was a nice balance: we still had to test squares, but the search felt informed rather than random.
- The scoring does create a real timing challenge: if the cave is far from a distant pirate, that pirate may simply run out of turns even after the cave is found. That’s not a bug, but it does mean the team should keep moving toward the likely region even before the cave is confirmed.

We didn’t encounter any rules issue or ambiguity that affected the game.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
One thing the designers might want to consider: a pirate can be mathematically locked out by starting position.

I started at A1, and the cave turned out to be J10 — 18 steps away. Since each pirate only gets 15 turns, I could never have reached it even if the cave had been found on turn 1. In our actual game P1 found it quite early and alerted everyone, but I was only at C1 and still needed 16 steps to J10, so entering was impossible. That made our crew’s score depend partly on random starting locations, not just on how well we coordinated.

Maybe that's intentional risk/pressure, but it felt a little frustrating because our strategy worked — we triangulated, moved toward the likely area, and found the cave — yet one pirate was doomed from the start.

Otherwise, the game felt fair and the scroll/sharing/alert mechanics worked well.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

Wait, I need to be careful about coordinate convention. Columns A-J (A=1 west to J=10 east). Rows 1-10 (1 south, 10 north). Manhattan distance.

I10 = (I=9, row 10).
A10 = (A=1, row 10).

P1's reading of I10 = 1 means treasure is within 1-5 of I10 (since noise can be off by up to 4, never below 1... wait if reading is 1, actual could be 1,2,3,4,5). Our position J1. We could dig along the J column, or head to somewhere useful. Since P1 is at I10 (distance 1 reported, so treasure is within 5 of I10), the treasure is likely in the northeast area. Our J1 dig said 6 away (actual 2-10). 

We have 15 turns; this is turn 2 of ours. We should move toward the candidates / triangulate.

Let's think about what's efficient. We could dig a few squares sharing readings to help triangulate. But we only get 15 turns, and each dig gives info. We want to eventually enter the cave, and ideally all pirates enter for max score. But there's a benefit to entering early (10 per turn left). However, all pirates must enter for score? Actually score is "100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing." So crew score = sum over pirates of (100 + 10 * turns left at entry), for those who enter. If one pirate never enters, that pirate brings nothing but the others still bring their bounty? "You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score." Hmm, probably each pirate's own contribution? Every pirate gets the same score = same score for all crew members, presumably the total bounty divided? Let me not overthink; goal is maximize total bounty = for each entering pirate, 100 + 10*turns left. So all four should enter, and enter early.

The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns. So if cave is found early, everyone can go enter and get 100 + 10*turns-left each.

Our job now: help find the cave and then go enter it.

Let's reason about the treasure location using readings.

True treasure T = (c, r).

- J1 (10,1): reported 6. Actual d4 = |c-10| + |r-1| ∈ [2,10].

Let's intersect these as actual distance constraints (we don't know actual but must be within these ranges).

Let's enumerate candidate squares satisfying all constraints? Let's do it.

c+r ≥ 12 and r ≤ c+1 and d1 ≤ 5 (near I10) etc.

r=5: c≥4 but d1 c=9 only → (9,5).

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
The design was clear and fun to play; the shared scroll system made the treasure hunt feel like a real crew effort. A few things worth noting for future runs:

1. **Alert timing / walking commitment** was a little tricky. When we committed to a long `go_to`, we couldn't see new non-alert scroll lines until we arrived, which made it hard to react to new readings. That made us more cautious about long walks, and encouraged hopping to nearby squares even when a farther square seemed more informative.

2. **The scoring reward slightly punishes long searches.** Since bounty includes turns left at entry, there's a tension between exploring carefully and rushing to enter once the cave is found. Early alerts are very powerful; we only scored 490 because three pirates arrived/entered at different times. That felt fair, but also meant the last pirate's bounty could vary a lot based on how far they were from the cave when it was found.

3. **Readings with ±4 noise** gave us a broad candidate set. We used rulers/mental enumeration from the shared readings; it worked well. If the intent was to make triangulation easier, the current noise level is fine; if it was meant to be the main puzzle, maybe allow players to "roughly locate" a small region earlier.

4. **A way to optionally mark a "best guess" or set a rendezvous square** on the scroll could reduce spelling things out in free text. But the 200-character say lines were enough.

5. **No issues with fairness or hidden information** came up; we only used what the game showed us.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.
- Find the cave only from your own digs and the scroll; using anything else the game shows you, such as its internal state or tools not meant for players, breaks the rules.
- When the game ends, each of you will be asked how your crew found the cave, and your crew's strategy will be judged: a crew found to have broken the rules is disqualified and scores zero.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
